newsitem.title: USA: Clinton names John Hope Franklin to head race panel.
newsitem.headline: Clinton names John Hope Franklin to head race panel.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday named retired historian John Hope Franklin to head an advisory panel that will examine racial problems in America.
Clinton appointed Franklin and six other members to a board that will counsel the president on his initiative to promote a national dialogue on controversial issues surrounding race.
Franklin, of Durham, N.C., is a retired historian to whom Clinton awarded a Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1995. He authored the landmark 1946 study, "From Slavery to Freedom."

Clinton also named to the panel William Winter, a former governor of Mississippi; Linda Chavez-Thompson, executive vice president of the AFL-CIO union; Robert Thomas, president and chief executive officer of Nissan USA; Angela Oh, a Calfornian involved in repairing race relations after Los Angeles riots; former New Jersey Gov. Thomas Kean, and Suzan Johnson Cook, senior pastor of Bronx Christian Fellowship Church in New York.
The panel was one element of Clinton's pledge to lead a year-long initiative on race. He is to discuss the effort in a speech Saturday at the University of California of San Diego.
